theme: The storm; Jairus; Peter’s confession; the Transfiguration
readingInstruction: Read Luke 8:22-9:50. A storm stilled, a girl raised, the Twelve sent out, Peter’s confession, the Transfiguration. This section turns on one question: who is Jesus?
settingTheScene: Jesus now shows his power over nature, demons, sickness, and death. Then, in chapter 9, the question of his identity moves to the center. Herod wonders who he is, the crowds guess, Peter answers. Right after the confession, Jesus speaks plainly of his coming suffering and the cost of following him. Eight days later, three disciples see his glory on the mountain.
observation: “Daughter, your faith has made you well; go in peace” (8:48).
“Do not fear; only believe, and she will be well” (8:50).
“But who do you say that I am?” Peter answered, “The Christ of God” (9:20).
“If anyone would come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow me” (9:23).
“This is my Son, my Chosen One; listen to him!” (9:35).
“For he who is least among you all is the one who is great” (9:48).
interpretation:
The storm on the lake shows who Jesus is. The disciples, some of them experienced fishermen, cry out that they are perishing. Jesus rebukes the wind and the waves, and there is calm. They ask, “Who then is this, that he commands even winds and water, and they obey him?” The Old Testament says only God does that (Psalm 107:29).

Then he crosses to the Gerasenes and frees a man possessed by many demons. The man, once naked and chained among the tombs, is found sitting at Jesus’ feet, clothed and in his right mind. When the people ask Jesus to leave, he tells the man to go home and declare how much God has done for him. The first missionary to the Gentiles was a former demoniac.

Jairus’s daughter and the woman with the flow of blood are woven together. The woman has been unclean and suffering for twelve years, and she touches the edge of his garment. Jesus stops, and calls her “Daughter.” A message comes that Jairus’s daughter has died. Jesus says, “Do not fear; only believe.” He takes her hand and says, “Child, arise,” and she does. Jesus is Lord over sickness and death.

The Twelve are sent out with power and authority. Herod hears and is perplexed. Jesus feeds the five thousand, and then asks the key question. The crowds say John, Elijah, or one of the prophets. Peter says, “The Christ of God.” Jesus warns them not to tell anyone yet, and speaks of suffering, rejection, death, and resurrection. Then he tells all who would follow that they must take up their cross daily. To follow the Christ is to follow the way of the cross.

Eight days later, on the mountain, Jesus is transfigured. Moses and Elijah speak with him about his “departure,” literally his exodus, which he will accomplish at Jerusalem. The voice from the cloud says, “This is my Son, my Chosen One; listen to him!” Then the disciples argue about who is greatest, and Jesus sets a child beside him. In the kingdom, greatness is humility.
connection: Psalm 107:23-30 describes the sea stilled by the LORD. Isaiah 53 is the suffering servant behind Jesus’ words about his death. Exodus 24 and 34 recall Moses on the mountain. Deuteronomy 18:15 told Israel to listen to the coming prophet. Matthew 16:13-28 and Mark 8:27-9:1 are the parallels. Romans 6:3-5 says we are united with Christ in his death and resurrection. Galatians 2:20 says, “I have been crucified with Christ.”
application:
Name the storm you are in. Bring it to Jesus as the disciples did, and hear him ask, “Where is your faith?”

Answer Jesus’ own question in your own words: “Who do you say that I am?”

Take up your cross daily. What does that mean today for your habits, your time, and your pride?
prayerPrompts: Say with Peter who Jesus is.
Tell him what storm you are facing.
Ask him to teach you to listen to him.
